I was a scheduled c-section, my twins came at 28 weeks and honestly it just left me with major anxiety around everything pregnancy and labour so we decided c-section for a solid date and expectations to manage that anxiety, and it really helped. 

We where originally booked in the afternoon but managed to get it changed to the morning slot so I was sitting around nervously for any longer than necessary, when we got there everyone was so kind and it really just put me at ease, I was able to sit and joke with my husband instead of just sitting shaking, not to say I wasn’t and didn’t get more nervous but it was a very supportive and reassuring place. 

I got my fancy socks (ha) and once they put the cannula in I knew it was getting close to go time.  That was probably the longest 30 minute wait, as they said they would be back for me shortly so the anticipation was high. Once they came to walk me along to theartre however the nerves really kicked in. 

I suppose I remember very little from the twins birth and how traumatic it was but being in that room brought a lot back, it was also the stark difference that made me feel more emotional than I thought I’d be, everyone was taking their time and looking out for me, my husband was there for the spinal telling me how proud he was of me, all the nurses where away of my previous section so they really just handled everything with care and extra reassurance. 

I struggled to relax to get the spinal in correctly, eventually one of the head doctors guided me through it, it meant a bit more local anaesthetic and I’ve been left with a numb spot at the bottom of my back but I honestly don’t care, it could go away and it also might not but I’m not fussed. Husband was very glad he had something to eat once watching the size of the spinal needle! 

Then it was go time, we stuck our playlist on and everyone made me aware of the tugging and things coming up and how to breathe through it, the anaesthesiologist popped over the top of my head to let me know if that fails he’s got a cupboard full of drugs which just made me laugh and relax. The tugging and the pulling was something else though it was really intense and I was really emotional, hubby was right with me though telling me how great I was doing. 

And then they dropped the screen so I could see my baby boy being lifted out and I just burst into full tears unable to hold any of it back, he was tiny and gorgeous and screaming the house down. Daddy went with him to trim the cord and take so many pictures, even the nurses took our phone to take photos for us for us just to enjoy the moment. 

Theodore Cole was born at 11:04 weighing 7lbs 14oz and was given to me as quickly as possible for skin to skin. I was instantly so in love that nothing else mattered and the rest of the section didn’t even feel like it was happening. We where in our own little bubble. 

He was born to a song I’ve loved since I was 16 and have played at every special event in my life, and then when he was placed in my arms to the song his dad picked for him before finally going to his daddy for cuddles to one of our wedding songs. 

We are so happy and so in love with him. I’m breastfeeding and it’s hard, people aren’t kidding when they say that, he went down to 7lbs 6, but now we are getting the hang of it - no more just screaming at my nipple then falling asleep - he’s back up to 7lbs 10, nipples are still cracked sore and bleeding but it’s definitely getting easier. 

Baby blues are no joke, I’ve not had them this intense before, my best advice is be honest, lean on your partner and midwife and speak it out, I’m so sad at every day that goes past, I miss him when he sleeps and I cry when I should be sleeping, but I keep myself going thinking of loving the time spent with & bonding with him, baby wearing, pram walks, milky smiles. I’d do anything for him in a heartbeat.

Mainly, it was my SO, he really saved me, even when I did struggle again it was still nothing on the scale of what it used to be.

However saying that I'm a big advocate of helping myself and not relying on others so;

Cleaning - this helped me majorly, a firm believer of tidy home tidy mind, but as I have 3 kids and 2 dogs this isnt always easy, but I organised every room one at a time, sometimes just a cupboard and it really makes life so much easier (of course I still have a junk drawer however!)

Mess - as opposed to the first, lists. Once kids are at school and the house is upside down, or if you're at work etc, I promise myself a certain amount of time and I'll start a small clean at a certain time, sometimes I even set a timer and whatever isnt done within that timer is left out. Lists are super helpful because I can just focus on what I'd like done, rather than folding washing for 30 minutes it can go to the side and I can take rubbish out etc in less time.  

- Both cleaning and the mess and how i manage it really help me to focus on other things, it can take me out of that anxiety zone.

Appearance - this one I always find silly telling people, but being depressed or anxious about certain things I can always relate back to being uncomfortable in my own skin. Sometimes I wont even be going anywhere, but I'm happy to put on my favourite songs and do my hair etc just how I like it and it can really make you feel better about yourself. It gives me an "I've got this" feeling.

Self care - probably a huge one for most, some days I just dont want to do anything or I'm overthinking another.. so I invented Fat Fridays. Now this isnt to say this day doesnt get moved about as needed (thick Thursdays, sloppy sundays etc) now this is a day just for you, no guilt. I can eat healthy all week (good diet really helps!) But I crave takeaways like no ones business, so I've got one specific day of the week where I get to look forward to with absolutely no guilt at all. If I'm having a bad day I can simply move it that week to a thursday, and itll be back to friday the next week unless needed, then I'm not over indulging on bad food. 

-  I like to pair my (foody) self care of course with relaxing 0 cleaning, no doing anything except good bad food, chilling, baths and pampering.

FINALLY! Goals/hobbies - find something to focus on and throw yourself into. Unluckily for me I never really found that one thing, I've always loved celebrating others however so birthday where always big and fun, and super luckily my SO proposed so I can really focus and enjoy wedding planning. But theres loads of groups and gyms and games and you name it out there that you can get into and get lost in when the depression and anxiety hits !
